run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:39:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects a real, rising error signal on the proxy's own inbound spans. frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR rose from about 2.4 per 10 minutes (samples 00:16:49 and 00:21:49) to 65.3 (10m ending 00:41:49), 161.1 (00:46:49) and 156.8 (00:51:49), and those spans are HTTP 504 with otel.status_code=ERROR lasting ~15.0 s (the proxy's route timeout). Trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20 (~00:47:26) shows the mechanism: load-generator user_checkout_single -> frontend POST /api/checkout 15.72 s -> checkout PlaceOrder 15.72 s -> checkout 'orders publish' 15.58 s; the frontend answered 200 only after the proxy had already returned 504. checkout 'orders publish' latency jumped from all-365-spans-under-100ms in the 10 minutes ending 00:36:49 to roughly 150 of 258 spans over 15 s in the 10 minutes ending 00:46:49, and checkout logged Kafka 'connection refused' during 00:37:57-00:38:09. The Kafka workload was restarted at 00:36:37 (new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485, pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:36:37Z, otherwise identical template/image), and the broker came up with freshly initialised topics at 00:38:16-00:38:18. The only switched-on fault-injection setting found in the environment is ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json: flag kafkaQueueProblems defaultVariant 'on' (variants off=0/on=100, description 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'); every other fault flag defaults to 'off'. A hypothesis (not directly observed) is that this setting is the fault behind the Kafka produce stalls and hence the proxy 504s; the restart of Deployment kafka is the visible mechanism, and neither the moment the flag changed nor the trigger of the restart can be established from this Run. Also observed but not tied to this cause: fraud-detection pod OOMKilled (exit 137) at 00:29:42 with a BackOff event, and low-rate steady flagd EventStream error spans on ad/recommendation that were flat before and during the incident.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans rose steeply inside the window: increase over 10m of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 2.37 (sample 00:16:49), 2.14 (00:21:49), 5.26 (00:26:49), 10.53 (00:31:49), 12.63 (00:36:49), 65.26 (00:41:49), 161.05 (00:46:49) and 156.79 (00:51:49); the 5m-rate query for the same service shows ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR going from 0 at 00:16:08 to 0.3889/s at 00:47:08.

The erroring frontend-proxy spans are HTTP 504: sampled rows show operation 'ingress' with status tags {error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR"} and duration_us ~15,000,000, each matched by a sibling 'router frontend egress' span of the same 15.0 s with status tags {error="true", http.status_code="0"}.

Trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20 (start ~00:47:26) contains: load-generator user_checkout_single 15.17 s -> load-generator POST 15.00 s with http.status_code 504 -> frontend-proxy ingress 15.00 s ERROR/504 -> frontend POST /api/checkout 15.72 s http.status_code 200 -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 15.72 s (rpc.grpc.status_code 0) -> checkout 'orders publish' 15.58 s; all other checkout child spans (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping/quote, payment, email) were tens of milliseconds.

checkout span 'orders publish' changed abruptly: in the 10 minutes ending 00:36:49 all 365 spans were at or below 100 ms (le=100.0 and le=+Inf both 365.26); in the 10 minutes ending 00:46:49 there were 258.12 spans total, 24.21 at or below 10 s and 108.47 at or below 15 s, i.e. about 150 spans above 15 s; in the 10 minutes ending 00:51:49 there were 228.25 spans total, 5.33 at or below 10 s and 76.80 at or below 15 s, i.e. about 151 above 15 s (buckets are cumulative; differences computed between le=+Inf and le=15000.0).

Over the 30 minutes ending 00:51:49 the largest error-span increases were frontend-proxy 'ingress' 234.95 and checkout 'orders publish' 14.70, followed by recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 3.05 and ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 2.03; the returned frontend, payment, cart, currency and product-catalog series in that top-25 list showed 0 increase (the list was truncated at 25 series, other series unknown).

checkout-5dccddf8bb-6qppz logged Kafka connectivity failures: 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused' repeatedly at 00:37:57-00:38:09, 'Failed to write message: kafka: client has run out of available brokers...' and 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', then 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092' at 00:38:22.

Deployment kafka was rollout-restarted: ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 was created 00:36:37 with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:36:37Z, pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 was created/started 00:36:37-00:36:38, the old pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 got 'Stopping container kafka' at 00:36:39, with ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet events. Apart from the restartedAt annotation the two ReplicaSet pod templates are identical (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, same env, same resources cpu 400m/memory 900Mi limits, no volumes).

kafka broker logs show a fresh broker start after the restart: leader initialisation for __consumer_offsets partitions and 'Leader orders-0 ... starts at leader epoch 0 from offset 0 ... high watermark 0, ISR [1]' at 00:38:18, plus consumer group assignments for groups fraud-detection and accounting at 00:38:19-00:38:21.

Deployment kafka carries deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2 and Deployment flagd also carries revision=2; both still reference unchanged images (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka and ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8), and the flagd pod flagd-f546d44c9-zx5qq was created 00:05:18 with 0 restarts.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) holds flag kafkaQueueProblems with defaultVariant "on" and variants {"off":0,"on":100}, described as 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'; the other fault flags in the same document — adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure — all have defaultVariant "off".

The character of the proxy error spans changed with the Kafka restart: before the 5m window ending 00:41:49 every frontend-proxy ingress error span was at or below 1400 ms (5.56, 5.56 and 7.78 per 5m at samples 00:26:49, 00:31:49, 00:36:49), while in the 5m ending 00:41:49 there were 61.11 error spans of which only 15.56 were at or below 15 s, and in the 5m ending 00:46:49 95.56 total with 21.11 at or below 15 s.

In the 10 minutes ending 00:36:49 (before the broker restart) the only notable error sources were frontend-proxy 'ingress' 12.63 and steady flagd EventStream errors on ad 1.05 and recommendation 1.05; frontend, checkout, payment, cart and the other returned services showed 0 error increase in that top-15 list.

frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 is Running and ready with 0 restarts, and in the sampled traces its upstream frontend spans for the same requests record http.status_code 200 (e.g. POST /api/checkout 15.72 s, GET /api/cart 2.4 s, GET / 4.5 s), so the proxy process itself was not restarting.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm has restarts=2 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 00:25:43 and finishedAt 00:29:42, and a BackOff event 'Back-off restarting failed container fraud-detection' at 00:29:43; its container memory working set (max_over_time 5m) peaked at 968.6 MiB at the 00:26:49 sample.

The restarted broker pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 used 0.284 cores over the 5 minutes ending 00:41:49 (container CPU limit is 400m), versus 0.029-0.037 cores for the previous kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 in earlier samples, and its memory working set was ~1174 MiB at the 00:41:49 sample.

The switched-on flag kafkaQueueProblems (defaultVariant 'on', value 100) is the injected fault behind the Kafka-side degradation: checkout's 'orders publish' stalls above 15 s and the Kafka connect/write failures, which in turn make /api/checkout exceed the proxy's 15 s route timeout and produce the frontend-proxy 504 error spans that drive RequestErrorRate. This is supported by the flag's own description and by the fact that the only slow segment in the traced checkout request is the Kafka publish, but the declared queue overload / consumer-side delay itself was not observed.

The kubectl rollout restart of Deployment kafka at 00:36:37 (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) is the visible trigger of the step change: the broker restarted with no persistent volume, reinitialised orders-0 at offset 0, checkout lost its broker connection 00:37:57-00:38:22, and 'orders publish' latency went from all-under-100ms to mostly-over-15s in the following ten minutes. The restart is a mechanism, and what triggered it (who ran the restart and why) is not visible in this Run.

The orders consumer side may also have been disturbed: fraud-detection is a member of the 'fraud-detection' consumer group on the orders topic and its container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 00:29:42 and restarted twice, which could have contributed to orders-topic lag; no evidence in this Run ties that OOM to the kafkaQueueProblems setting or to the proxy 504s.

The low-rate ingress errors that appeared around 00:22-00:36 (about 5-8 per 5 minutes, all at or below 1.4 s) are a separate, unexplained phenomenon: no backend service reported error spans in that period, so they may be generated by the proxy itself (e.g. unmatched routes/4xx) and are not shown to be part of the 15 s-timeout failure.

checkout 'orders publish' was fast before the Kafka restart (all 365 spans at or below 100 ms in the 10 minutes ending 00:36:49) while the kafkaQueueProblems flag is read as 'on' in the current ConfigMap; therefore the flag's on-state alone does not by itself explain the onset timing, and the restart at 00:36:37 remains a competing explanation for the step change.

ad and recommendation flagd EventStream error spans stayed essentially flat across the baseline and the incident (1.05 per 10m at 00:36:49 and 00:51:49 for ad; 1.18, 1.07 and 1.07 per 10m for recommendation at 00:16:49, 00:21:49 and 00:51:49), so they look like pre-existing background rather than part of this alert.

Rejected as the cause: a crash or failure of the frontend-proxy process itself. The pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts, and every erroring ingress span is a 504 paired with an egress span that received no HTTP response while the upstream frontend span records http.status_code 200 after ~15.7 s — the proxy reports the timeout, it does not originate the failure.

Rejected as the cause: an application-level error in the frontend or the other checkout dependencies. In the sampled failing trace the frontend, cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping/quote, payment and email spans all carry success statuses (http 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code 0) and only 'orders publish' is slow, and the returned frontend/payment/cart/currency/product-catalog error series show 0 increase over 30m.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the moment ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config switched kafkaQueueProblems to 'on', and who or what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:36:37Z to Deployment kafka, cannot be determined.

The declared fault itself (Kafka queue overload / consumer-side delay) was not directly observed: a metric-name query for kafka.*, *queue.* and *lag.* patterns returned no data (query matched nothing), so broker queue depth, consumer-group lag and message counts could not be measured.
The RequestErrorRate alert rule and the annotation's 'current: 0.4' could not be verified: list_prometheus_rules returned no data, so the alert's exact expression and ratio definition are unknown.

The character of the pre-restart ingress errors (5-8 per 5 minutes, all at or below 1.4 s, starting around 00:22-00:26) is unknown; a traces_search_by_tags query for frontend-proxy error spans of >=14 s in 00:18-00:34 returned no data (no trace matched), and Jaeger keeps only recent traces, so earlier traces may simply be absent.

Whether the fraud-detection OOMKilled restarts (exit 137, 00:29:42) are related to the Kafka degradation is unresolved; a log query on that pod for flag/kafka/delay/error/memory/orders keywords returned no data (no matching lines shown), so its consumer behaviour is unknown.

Kafka broker logs were read only up to a bounded number of lines per query (145 matching lines, newest 40 shown), so the absence of post-restart WARN/ERROR lines is not established; only the logged startup sequence and group assignments were observed.

No Jaeger operations are recorded under the 'kafka' service name (traces_list_operations returned no data), so the broker's own tracing is unavailable and the producer/consumer behaviour must be inferred from checkout logs and spans.

Trace evidence is a biased sample and covers only recent traces (source times around 00:47); spans and traces not returned remain unknown, and no complete call chain for the 15 s-timeout requests before 00:47 could be reconstructed.

Kubernetes object state is the state at query time; the pre-00:36 pod set and the exact Deployment/ConfigMap history inside the window could not be replayed, and the older container instance logs of kafka and checkout were unavailable (previous instance not found).
next_steps: Review flagd-config change history / GitOps or Helm values for otel-demo to establish when kafkaQueueProblems was set to 'on' and whether it is intended to stay on.
Identify who or what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:36:37Z to Deployment kafka, and whether the restart was a response to earlier symptoms.
Verify the alert expression for RequestErrorRate and whether its 0.4 reading is a ratio or a rate, then compare with the frontend-proxy ingress error spans observed here.

Add or check Kafka broker/consumer metrics (queue depth, consumer-group lag, request latency) to confirm the overload/lag hypothesis directly, and check whether fraud-detection's memory use and OOMKills track Kafka load.
If the injected fault is confirmed as unintended, disable the kafkaQueueProblems flag and re-check checkout 'orders publish' latency and frontend-proxy 504 rate.

The pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts, and every erroring ingress span is a 504 paired with an egress span that received no HTTP response while the upstream frontend span records http.status_code 200 after ~15.7 s — the proxy reports the timeout, it does not originate the failure.

Rejected as the cause: an application-level error in the frontend or the other checkout dependencies. In the sampled failing trace the frontend, cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping/quote, payment and email spans all carry success statuses (http 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code 0) and only 'orders publish' is slow, and the returned frontend/payment/cart/currency/product-catalog error series show 0 increase over 30m.
